wages.authority: Wage Committee Notice on Minimum Wage Rate No.14 (17 June 2025, Royal Gazette vol.142 special 236D, in force 1 July 2025; https://www.mol.go.th/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/07/%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A8-%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%88.%E0%B8%82%E0%B8%B1%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%95%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B3-%E0%B8%8914-%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%A1.pdf and the Ministry's printed table): cls.2(3)–18 a daily rate for each of the 77 provinces, cl.2(3) Ko Samui and cl.3 Mueang Chiang Mai and Hat Yai overriding their province; cl.2(1)–(2) THB400 nationwide for hotels of type 2–4 (Ministerial Regulation on hotel categories No.2 B.E.2566) and Service Establishment Act businesses; the higher applicable rate binds. cl.19: the day is the normal working day (at most 7 hours hazardous, 8 otherwise), however much shorter the employer makes it; cl.20: no employer may pay less, so a shortfall blocks the run. The table is compared on each normal working day of every contract at the worksite and sector its terms record that day; no Act or Ministry text read converts the daily rate to a monthly comparator, so by_region stays empty. Owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-WAGE-01): the law being silent, a monthly wage is held to the daily rate × 30 — each normal working day at monthly ÷ ordinary_divisor_days (30, LPA s.68's conversion) against that day's worksite rate; lawful because it is the Act's only stated month-to-day conversion and cl.20 is met on every day compared. A semi-monthly base_salary is its month; a weekly wage is taken to its month (× 52 ÷ 12) before the divisor.

encashment.authority: Labour Protection Act s.67 (as amended by No.2 B.E.2551): on termination the employer pays wages for the annual leave owed — the year of termination pro rata where the employer terminates other than under s.119, and carried-forward leave in every case — at the wage rate in force at termination. A monthly wage’s day is taken as monthly wage ÷ 30, the Act’s own conversion of a month (s.68, stated for overtime and holiday pay); no text read states another divisor for leave pay (register TH-WORK-05, TH-EXIT-02).

work_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 (Council of State consolidation through No.9 B.E.2568, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/ZGN3NXk0eENvNjBSdjRnT2NsdjFTQT09): s.23 normal hours at most eight a day (seven for work declared hazardous on dated employment terms); s.28 a weekly holiday; s.29 a traditional holiday falling on a weekly holiday moves to the next working day (SUBSTITUTE); s.56 weekly-holiday wages are owed except to employees paid daily, hourly or by piece; traditional and annual holidays are paid to all; s.61 overtime on a working day at least 1.5× the hourly rate; s.62 work on a holiday — (1) at least 1× more for an employee entitled to wages on that holiday, (2) at least 2× for one who is not (weekly holiday of a daily/hourly-paid employee); s.63 overtime on a holiday at least 3×; s.65(1)/s.66 an employee with authority to hire, reward or dismiss has no s.61–63 entitlement (read as work classification MANAGERIAL); s.65(2)–(9) (re-read 30 Sep 2026 in the consolidation) have no s.61 overtime or s.63 holiday-overtime pay unless the employer agrees, but keep s.62 holiday-work pay, and those in (3)–(9) are paid the working-day hourly rate for each hour worked beyond the normal hours: work classification COMMISSION_SALES (s.65(2), canvassing sales paid commission) is priced by band S65-OT-EXCLUDED at nothing and OVERTIME_AT_HOURLY_RATE (s.65(3)–(9): railway train operations, water gates, water-level reading, firefighting and public-danger prevention, outside work whose hours cannot be fixed, watch duty outside normal work, work a Ministerial Regulation adds) by band S65-OT-HOURLY-1.0X at 1× (register TH-WORK-06); an agreed higher rate is contractual, not modelled; s.68 the hourly rate of a monthly-paid employee is the monthly wage ÷ (30 × normal hours a day). The Act states no part-month proration: the seed prorates a monthly wage on calendar days, because s.56(1) pays a monthly wage for every day including weekly holidays, and deducts an unpaid day at the month’s calendar-day rate — a reading, not statute text (register TH-WORK-05). No statutory night premium exists (register TH-WORK-07). The Ministerial Regulation No.3 B.E.2541 combined 36-hour weekly overtime/holiday-work ceiling is transcribed; the timed s.27 adult breaks still need a saved compliance gate (register TH-WORK-07).

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Labour Protection Act s.70 para.2: where the employer terminates, wages and other money owed on termination are paid within three days of the termination.
Labour Protection Act s.70 para.1: otherwise wages are paid on the agreed pay day, at least once a month.

sources.instructions: Register: docs/inventory/thailand.csv. On 28 September 2026 the ratchakitcha.soc.go.th Gazette PDFs returned HTTP 403 to scripted and in-app browser fetches; on 29 September 2026 curl with a browser user agent received them. The s.33 base regulation was read from the rendered pages of the SSO’s copy of the Gazette (download_by_pool_file/47755, vol.142 part 81 Kor pp.5–6, 12 December 2025; its text layer is unreadable); the Employee Welfare Fund commencement decree (84794, vol.142 part 59 Kor, 14 September 2025) and rate regulation (86102, vol.142 part 60 Kor, 15 September 2025) from Internet Archive captures of the Gazette’s own PDFs; the flood-relief notice was read from the Gazette’s own PDF (100888, 47,741 bytes, SHA-256 1dcc3d4c…6c209f41ad, rendered page read 29 September 2026): Ministry of Labour notice under Social Security Act s.46/1 para.1, vol.143 special part 6 Ngor p.7, published 8 January 2026, signed 7 January 2026; cl.1 3% each side for a registered employer and its registered s.33 insured in the nine listed provinces, wage months December 2025–May 2026; cl.2 THB283 a month for a registered s.39 insured; cl.3 an overpayment is refunded on request at an SSO office.

facts.label: SSO flood-relief rate (southern provinces)
facts.description: Ministry of Labour notice under Social Security Act s.46/1, Gazette vol.143 special part 6 Ngor p.7, published 8 January 2026 (https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/100888.pdf, cl.1): a registered employer, and its s.33 insured employees, in Trang, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Narathiwat, Pattani, Phatthalung, Yala, Songkhla, Satun or Surat Thani contribute 3% each side instead of 5% for wage months December 2025–May 2026. Record the registration locality, not the worksite address; unrecorded is the ordinary 5%.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for a s.119 cause stated in the notice
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.119: no severance where the dismissal is for dishonesty or an intentional crime against the employer, wilful damage, serious negligence, a breach after a valid written warning, three consecutive working days’ absence without reason, or final imprisonment — and the cause was stated in the notice. s.67 then pays only carried-forward annual leave.

exit_facts.label: Fixed-term project, occasional or seasonal work finished within two years
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.118 paras 3–4: severance is not owed at the end of a written fixed-term contract for a special project outside the employer’s normal business, or for occasional or seasonal work, finished within two years. Every other contract expiry is a termination (s.118 para 2).

exit_facts.label: Objected in writing to a workplace relocation (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 para.3: within 30 days of the relocation notice (or of the move), the employee told the employer in writing that the move materially affects their or their family’s life and did not go; the contract ends on the move and special severance of at least the s.118 rate is owed. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Relocation notice posted 30 days ahead (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 paras 1–2: the employer posted the relocation notice at the workplace at least 30 days before the move; otherwise 30 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice to an employee who does not go. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for machinery or technology restructuring (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121: the termination follows a reorganisation of units, production, distribution or service because of machinery or a change of machinery or technology that reduces the workforce. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: 60 days’ notice given to the inspector and the employee (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121 para.1: the date, reason and employee list were notified to the labour inspector and the employee at least 60 days before the termination; otherwise 60 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice (para.2). Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Termination notice date (YYYY-MM-DD, s.17)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.17 para.2: the day the employer gave written notice ending the contract; it takes effect on the payday after the first payday on or after it. Blank or unrecorded is no notice: s.17/1 pay in lieu then runs from the removal.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: the recorded reason that dispenses with the worker’s consent for this overtime or holiday-work occasion.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception evidence
work_day_facts.description: The document proving the continuous-work necessity, the emergency or the s.25 business classification.

work_day_facts.label: Split-break agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27: the prior agreement to split the day’s hour of rest into shorter breaks.

work_day_facts.label: Under-18 night-work permission
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.47: when the Director-General’s written permission for under-18 night work was granted; its reference is the evidence.

work_day_facts.label: Normal-day redistribution agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: the worker’s prior agreement to a normal day above eight hours within the 48-hour week.

terms_facts.label: Hazardous work
terms_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: work the Ministerial Regulation declares hazardous to health or safety, limited to 7 normal hours a day and 42 a week. Default false: work is hazardous only as declared.

terms_facts.label: Pregnancy status
terms_facts.description: LPA s.39/1: the dated status read before night, overtime or holiday work is allowed.

obligations.description: Register each s.33 insured employee (aged 15–60 on entry) with the Social Security Office and report changes.
obligations.trigger: A new employee, a change of insured facts, or an exit.
obligations.timing: The insured list within 30 days of hiring; changes by the 15th of the following month.
obligations.authority: Social Security Act ss.33, 34, 44 (https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09); register TH-SS-12.

obligations.description: Deduct the employee share at every wage payment and remit both shares with the contribution return; 2% a month on late or short remittance from the day after the due date, at most the contribution owed (s.49 para.1 as amended by No.4 B.E.2558).
obligations.trigger: Each wage payment to an insured employee.
obligations.timing: By the 15th of the month after the deduction.
obligations.authority: Social Security Act ss.47, 49 (https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09); register TH-SS-01, TH-SS-12.

obligations.description: File the monthly ภ.ง.ด.1 withholding return and remit the s.50(1) tax withheld.
obligations.trigger: Each month with s.40(1) payments.
obligations.timing: Within 7 days after the month of payment (15 days if e-filed).
obligations.authority: Revenue Code ss.52, 58 (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-04.

obligations.description: File the annual ภ.ง.ด.1ก summary of s.40(1) payments and tax withheld.
obligations.trigger: Each tax year with s.40(1) payments.
obligations.timing: Within February of the following year (8 March if e-filed).
obligations.authority: Revenue Code s.58 (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-04.

obligations.description: Issue the two-copy s.50 bis withholding certificate to each payee.
obligations.trigger: Year end, or a departure during the year.
obligations.timing: By 15 February of the following year, or within one month after a departure.
obligations.authority: Revenue Code s.50 bis (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-09.

obligations.description: Pay wages, s.67 annual-leave pay, s.118 severance and ss.120–122 special severance on an employer termination (or a s.120 relocation objection), and s.17/1 pay in lieu of the missing s.17 notice (due on the day the employee leaves).
obligations.trigger: An employer termination.
obligations.timing: Within three days of termination (s.70 para.2).
obligations.authority: Labour Protection Act ss.17, 67, 70, 118–122 (https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/ZGN3NXk0eENvNjBSdjRnT2NsdjFTQT09); register TH-EXIT-01–07.

facts.label: SSO flood-relief rate (southern provinces)

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for a s.119 cause stated in the notice
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.119: no severance where the dismissal is for dishonesty or an intentional crime against the employer, wilful damage, serious negligence, a breach after a valid written warning, three consecutive working days’ absence without reason, or final imprisonment — and the cause was stated in the notice. s.67 then pays only carried-forward annual leave.

exit_facts.label: Fixed-term project, occasional or seasonal work finished within two years
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.118 paras 3–4: severance is not owed at the end of a written fixed-term contract for a special project outside the employer’s normal business, or for occasional or seasonal work, finished within two years. Every other contract expiry is a termination (s.118 para 2).

exit_facts.label: Objected in writing to a workplace relocation (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 para.3: within 30 days of the relocation notice (or of the move), the employee told the employer in writing that the move materially affects their or their family’s life and did not go; the contract ends on the move and special severance of at least the s.118 rate is owed. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Relocation notice posted 30 days ahead (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 paras 1–2: the employer posted the relocation notice at the workplace at least 30 days before the move; otherwise 30 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice to an employee who does not go. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for machinery or technology restructuring (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121: the termination follows a reorganisation of units, production, distribution or service because of machinery or a change of machinery or technology that reduces the workforce. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: 60 days’ notice given to the inspector and the employee (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121 para.1: the date, reason and employee list were notified to the labour inspector and the employee at least 60 days before the termination; otherwise 60 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice (para.2). Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Termination notice date (YYYY-MM-DD, s.17)

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception evidence

work_day_facts.label: Split-break agreement

work_day_facts.label: Under-18 night-work permission

work_day_facts.label: Normal-day redistribution agreement

terms_facts.label: Hazardous work

terms_facts.label: Pregnancy status
terms_facts.description: LPA s.39/1: the dated status read before night, overtime or holiday work is allowed.

obligations.description: Deduct the employee share at every wage payment and remit both shares with the contribution return; 2% a month on late or short remittance from the day after the due date, at most the contribution owed (s.49 para.1 as amended by No.4 B.E.2558).

obligations.timing: By the 15th of the month after the deduction.
obligations.authority: Social Security Act ss.47, 49 (https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09); register TH-SS-01, TH-SS-12.

obligations.description: File the monthly ภ.ง.ด.1 withholding return and remit the s.50(1) tax withheld.
obligations.trigger: Each month with s.40(1) payments.
obligations.timing: Within 7 days after the month of payment (15 days if e-filed).
obligations.authority: Revenue Code ss.52, 58 (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-04.

obligations.description: File the annual ภ.ง.ด.1ก summary of s.40(1) payments and tax withheld.
obligations.trigger: Each tax year with s.40(1) payments.
obligations.timing: Within February of the following year (8 March if e-filed).
obligations.authority: Revenue Code s.58 (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-04.

obligations.description: Issue the two-copy s.50 bis withholding certificate to each payee.
obligations.trigger: Year end, or a departure during the year.
obligations.timing: By 15 February of the following year, or within one month after a departure.
obligations.authority: Revenue Code s.50 bis (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html); register TH-PIT-09.

obligations.description: Pay wages, s.67 annual-leave pay, s.118 severance and ss.120–122 special severance on an employer termination (or a s.120 relocation objection), and s.17/1 pay in lieu of the missing s.17 notice (due on the day the employee leaves).
obligations.trigger: An employer termination.
obligations.timing: Within three days of termination (s.70 para.2).

day_rules.message: cannot perform Thai night or holiday work while pregnant
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.39/1 para.1.

day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.39/1 para.2: working-day overtime only in executive, academic, clerical or financial work that does not affect her health.

day_rules.message: needs Thai s.27 wage treatment for rest over two hours

day_rules.message: worked over five consecutive hours without a timed Thai s.27 break
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1: a rest of at least one hour after no more than five consecutive working hours.

day_rules.message: needs a timed hour of Thai s.27 rest
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1.

day_rules.message: needs a prior split-break agreement for Thai s.27 rest
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1: the hour may be split into shorter breaks only by prior agreement, totalling at least one hour a day.

day_rules.message: needs a timed 20-minute rest before Thai overtime of at least two hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.3: a rest of at least 20 minutes before overtime of two hours or more.

day_rules.message: needs timed work and rest records for the Thai under-18 shift
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.46–48: the young-worker rest, night and overtime rules are judged on the timed day.

day_rules.message: cannot work on a Thai holiday while under 18
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.48: no employee under 18 may work overtime or on a holiday.

day_rules.message: needs prior written Thai Director-General permission for under-18 night work
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.47: no employee under 18 may work 22:00–06:00 without the Director-General’s prior written permission.

day_rules.message: needs a continuous 60-minute rest after at most four hours of Thai under-18 work
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.46: a young employee rests at least one continuous hour a day after no more than four hours of work.

day_rules.message: needs Thai s.27 wage treatment for rest over two hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.4.

day_rules.message: needs a continuous 60-minute rest on the Thai under-18 workday
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.46.

day_rules.message: cannot work overtime in Thailand while under 18
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.48.

day_rules.message: needs evidence for the Thai consent exception
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: an occasion without consent needs its recorded necessity, emergency or s.25 business.

day_rules.message: cannot use a Thai holiday-work exception on an ordinary day
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.25 para.2: the listed businesses may require holiday work, not working-day overtime.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for a s.119 cause stated in the notice
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.119: no severance where the dismissal is for dishonesty or an intentional crime against the employer, wilful damage, serious negligence, a breach after a valid written warning, three consecutive working days’ absence without reason, or final imprisonment — and the cause was stated in the notice. s.67 then pays only carried-forward annual leave.

exit_facts.label: Fixed-term project, occasional or seasonal work finished within two years
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.118 paras 3–4: severance is not owed at the end of a written fixed-term contract for a special project outside the employer’s normal business, or for occasional or seasonal work, finished within two years. Every other contract expiry is a termination (s.118 para 2).

exit_facts.label: Objected in writing to a workplace relocation (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 para.3: within 30 days of the relocation notice (or of the move), the employee told the employer in writing that the move materially affects their or their family’s life and did not go; the contract ends on the move and special severance of at least the s.118 rate is owed. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Relocation notice posted 30 days ahead (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 paras 1–2: the employer posted the relocation notice at the workplace at least 30 days before the move; otherwise 30 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice to an employee who does not go. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for machinery or technology restructuring (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121: the termination follows a reorganisation of units, production, distribution or service because of machinery or a change of machinery or technology that reduces the workforce. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: 60 days’ notice given to the inspector and the employee (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121 para.1: the date, reason and employee list were notified to the labour inspector and the employee at least 60 days before the termination; otherwise 60 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice (para.2). Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Termination notice date (YYYY-MM-DD, s.17)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.17 para.2: the day the employer gave written notice ending the contract; it takes effect on the payday after the first payday on or after it. Blank or unrecorded is no notice: s.17/1 pay in lieu then runs from the removal.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: the recorded reason that dispenses with the worker’s consent for this overtime or holiday-work occasion.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception evidence
work_day_facts.description: The document proving the continuous-work necessity, the emergency or the s.25 business classification.

work_day_facts.label: Split-break agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27: the prior agreement to split the day’s hour of rest into shorter breaks.

work_day_facts.label: Under-18 night-work permission

work_day_facts.label: Normal-day redistribution agreement

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for a s.119 cause stated in the notice
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.119: no severance where the dismissal is for dishonesty or an intentional crime against the employer, wilful damage, serious negligence, a breach after a valid written warning, three consecutive working days’ absence without reason, or final imprisonment — and the cause was stated in the notice. s.67 then pays only carried-forward annual leave.

exit_facts.label: Fixed-term project, occasional or seasonal work finished within two years
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.118 paras 3–4: severance is not owed at the end of a written fixed-term contract for a special project outside the employer’s normal business, or for occasional or seasonal work, finished within two years. Every other contract expiry is a termination (s.118 para 2).

exit_facts.label: Objected in writing to a workplace relocation (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 para.3: within 30 days of the relocation notice (or of the move), the employee told the employer in writing that the move materially affects their or their family’s life and did not go; the contract ends on the move and special severance of at least the s.118 rate is owed. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Relocation notice posted 30 days ahead (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 paras 1–2: the employer posted the relocation notice at the workplace at least 30 days before the move; otherwise 30 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice to an employee who does not go. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for machinery or technology restructuring (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121: the termination follows a reorganisation of units, production, distribution or service because of machinery or a change of machinery or technology that reduces the workforce. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: 60 days’ notice given to the inspector and the employee (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121 para.1: the date, reason and employee list were notified to the labour inspector and the employee at least 60 days before the termination; otherwise 60 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice (para.2). Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Termination notice date (YYYY-MM-DD, s.17)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.17 para.2: the day the employer gave written notice ending the contract; it takes effect on the payday after the first payday on or after it. Blank or unrecorded is no notice: s.17/1 pay in lieu then runs from the removal.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: the recorded reason that dispenses with the worker’s consent for this overtime or holiday-work occasion.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception evidence
work_day_facts.description: The document proving the continuous-work necessity, the emergency or the s.25 business classification.

work_day_facts.label: Split-break agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27: the prior agreement to split the day’s hour of rest into shorter breaks.

work_day_facts.label: Under-18 night-work permission
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.47: when the Director-General’s written permission for under-18 night work was granted; its reference is the evidence.

work_day_facts.label: Normal-day redistribution agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: the worker’s prior agreement to a normal day above eight hours within the 48-hour week.

terms_facts.label: Hazardous work
terms_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: work the Ministerial Regulation declares hazardous to health or safety, limited to 7 normal hours a day and 42 a week. Default false: work is hazardous only as declared.

terms_facts.label: Pregnancy status
terms_facts.description: LPA s.39/1: the dated status read before night, overtime or holiday work is allowed.

limits.authority: Labour Protection Act s.23: ordinary work is limited to 48 normal hours per week, including where an agreed redistribution extends a normal day to nine hours.
Labour Protection Act s.23: hazardous work is limited to 7 normal hours per day and 42 per week.
Labour Protection Act s.26 and Ministerial Regulation No.3 B.E.2541: overtime, holiday work and holiday overtime together may not exceed 36 hours in a week.
Labour Protection Act s.28: at least one weekly holiday, the interval between holidays not exceeding six days.

overtime_consent.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: each occasion of overtime or holiday work needs the employee’s prior consent, save continuous work whose stopping causes damage, an emergency, or the s.25 businesses’ holiday work.

day_rules.message: has a hazardous normal shift above the 7-hour limit
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act s.23: hazardous work is limited to 7 normal hours per day and 42 per week.

day_rules.message: cannot work overtime or on a holiday in Thai hazardous work

day_rules.message: needs a prior worker agreement for the redistributed normal day
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: a normal day above eight hours needs the worker’s prior agreement, within the 48-hour week.

day_rules.message: needs a separately priced 1.5× supplement for normal hours above eight

day_rules.message: needs Thai guard holiday normal-hour compensation
day_rules.authority: Guard-work regulation in force 24 April 2026 (https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/68372.pdf): the GUARD_NORMAL_SUPPLEMENT band prices a non-monthly guard's normal hours above eight on an ordinary day only; a holiday's is not configured.

day_rules.message: needs a birth date to check Thai young-worker hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.44–48: the young-worker protections turn on the worker being under 18.

day_rules.message: needs a dated Thai pregnancy status before night, overtime or holiday work
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.39/1: a pregnant employee may not work 22:00–06:00, overtime or on a holiday.

day_rules.message: cannot perform Thai night or holiday work while pregnant
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.39/1 para.1.

day_rules.message: needs supported Thai s.39/1 role and health evidence before pregnant working-day overtime
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.39/1 para.2: working-day overtime only in executive, academic, clerical or financial work that does not affect her health.

day_rules.message: needs Thai s.27 wage treatment for rest over two hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.4: rest beyond two hours a day counts as normal working time.

day_rules.message: worked over five consecutive hours without a timed Thai s.27 break
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1: a rest of at least one hour after no more than five consecutive working hours.

day_rules.message: needs a timed hour of Thai s.27 rest
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1.

day_rules.message: needs a prior split-break agreement for Thai s.27 rest
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.1: the hour may be split into shorter breaks only by prior agreement, totalling at least one hour a day.

day_rules.message: needs a timed 20-minute rest before Thai overtime of at least two hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.3: a rest of at least 20 minutes before overtime of two hours or more.

day_rules.message: needs timed work and rest records for the Thai under-18 shift
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.46–48: the young-worker rest, night and overtime rules are judged on the timed day.

day_rules.message: cannot work on a Thai holiday while under 18
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.48: no employee under 18 may work overtime or on a holiday.

day_rules.message: needs prior written Thai Director-General permission for under-18 night work
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.47: no employee under 18 may work 22:00–06:00 without the Director-General’s prior written permission.

day_rules.message: needs a continuous 60-minute rest after at most four hours of Thai under-18 work
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.46: a young employee rests at least one continuous hour a day after no more than four hours of work.

day_rules.message: needs Thai s.27 wage treatment for rest over two hours
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27 para.4.

day_rules.message: needs a continuous 60-minute rest on the Thai under-18 workday
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.46.

day_rules.message: cannot work overtime in Thailand while under 18
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.48.

day_rules.message: needs evidence for the Thai consent exception
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: an occasion without consent needs its recorded necessity, emergency or s.25 business.

day_rules.message: cannot use a Thai holiday-work exception on an ordinary day
day_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.25 para.2: the listed businesses may require holiday work, not working-day overtime.

wages.authority: Wage Committee Notice on Minimum Wage Rate No.14 (17 June 2025, Royal Gazette vol.142 special 236D, in force 1 July 2025; https://www.mol.go.th/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/07/%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A8-%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%88.%E0%B8%82%E0%B8%B1%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%95%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B3-%E0%B8%8914-%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%A1.pdf and the Ministry's printed table): cls.2(3)–18 a daily rate for each of the 77 provinces, cl.2(3) Ko Samui and cl.3 Mueang Chiang Mai and Hat Yai overriding their province; cl.2(1)–(2) THB400 nationwide for hotels of type 2–4 (Ministerial Regulation on hotel categories No.2 B.E.2566) and Service Establishment Act businesses; the higher applicable rate binds. cl.19: the day is the normal working day (at most 7 hours hazardous, 8 otherwise), however much shorter the employer makes it; cl.20: no employer may pay less, so a shortfall blocks the run. The table is compared on each normal working day of every contract at the worksite and sector its terms record that day; no Act or Ministry text read converts the daily rate to a monthly comparator, so by_region stays empty. Owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-WAGE-01): the law being silent, a monthly wage is held to the daily rate × 30 — each normal working day at monthly ÷ ordinary_divisor_days (30, LPA s.68's conversion) against that day's worksite rate; lawful because it is the Act's only stated month-to-day conversion and cl.20 is met on every day compared. A semi-monthly base_salary is its month; a weekly wage is taken to its month (× 52 ÷ 12) before the divisor.

encashment.authority: Labour Protection Act s.67 (as amended by No.2 B.E.2551): on termination the employer pays wages for the annual leave owed — the year of termination pro rata where the employer terminates other than under s.119, and carried-forward leave in every case — at the wage rate in force at termination. A monthly wage’s day is taken as monthly wage ÷ 30, the Act’s own conversion of a month (s.68, stated for overtime and holiday pay); no text read states another divisor for leave pay (register TH-WORK-05, TH-EXIT-02).

work_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 (Council of State consolidation through No.9 B.E.2568, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/ZGN3NXk0eENvNjBSdjRnT2NsdjFTQT09): s.23 normal hours at most eight a day (seven for work declared hazardous on dated employment terms); s.28 a weekly holiday; s.29 a traditional holiday falling on a weekly holiday moves to the next working day (SUBSTITUTE); s.56 weekly-holiday wages are owed except to employees paid daily, hourly or by piece; traditional and annual holidays are paid to all; s.61 overtime on a working day at least 1.5× the hourly rate; s.62 work on a holiday — (1) at least 1× more for an employee entitled to wages on that holiday, (2) at least 2× for one who is not (weekly holiday of a daily/hourly-paid employee); s.63 overtime on a holiday at least 3×; s.65(1)/s.66 an employee with authority to hire, reward or dismiss has no s.61–63 entitlement (read as work classification MANAGERIAL); s.65(2)–(9) (re-read 30 Sep 2026 in the consolidation) have no s.61 overtime or s.63 holiday-overtime pay unless the employer agrees, but keep s.62 holiday-work pay, and those in (3)–(9) are paid the working-day hourly rate for each hour worked beyond the normal hours: work classification COMMISSION_SALES (s.65(2), canvassing sales paid commission) is priced by band S65-OT-EXCLUDED at nothing and OVERTIME_AT_HOURLY_RATE (s.65(3)–(9): railway train operations, water gates, water-level reading, firefighting and public-danger prevention, outside work whose hours cannot be fixed, watch duty outside normal work, work a Ministerial Regulation adds) by band S65-OT-HOURLY-1.0X at 1× (register TH-WORK-06); an agreed higher rate is contractual, not modelled; s.68 the hourly rate of a monthly-paid employee is the monthly wage ÷ (30 × normal hours a day). The Act states no part-month proration: the seed prorates a monthly wage on calendar days, because s.56(1) pays a monthly wage for every day including weekly holidays, and deducts an unpaid day at the month’s calendar-day rate — a reading, not statute text (register TH-WORK-05). No statutory night premium exists (register TH-WORK-07). The Ministerial Regulation No.3 B.E.2541 combined 36-hour weekly overtime/holiday-work ceiling is transcribed; the timed s.27 adult breaks still need a saved compliance gate (register TH-WORK-07).

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Labour Protection Act s.70 para.2: where the employer terminates, wages and other money owed on termination are paid within three days of the termination.
Labour Protection Act s.70 para.1: otherwise wages are paid on the agreed pay day, at least once a month.

wages.authority: Wage Committee Notice on Minimum Wage Rate No.14 (17 June 2025, Royal Gazette vol.142 special 236D, in force 1 July 2025; https://www.mol.go.th/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/07/%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A8-%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%88.%E0%B8%82%E0%B8%B1%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%95%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B3-%E0%B8%8914-%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%A1.pdf and the Ministry's printed table): cls.2(3)–18 a daily rate for each of the 77 provinces, cl.2(3) Ko Samui and cl.3 Mueang Chiang Mai and Hat Yai overriding their province; cl.2(1)–(2) THB400 nationwide for hotels of type 2–4 (Ministerial Regulation on hotel categories No.2 B.E.2566) and Service Establishment Act businesses; the higher applicable rate binds. cl.19: the day is the normal working day (at most 7 hours hazardous, 8 otherwise), however much shorter the employer makes it; cl.20: no employer may pay less, so a shortfall blocks the run. The table is compared on each normal working day of every contract at the worksite and sector its terms record that day; no Act or Ministry text read converts the daily rate to a monthly comparator, so by_region stays empty. Owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-WAGE-01): the law being silent, a monthly wage is held to the daily rate × 30 — each normal working day at monthly ÷ ordinary_divisor_days (30, LPA s.68's conversion) against that day's worksite rate; lawful because it is the Act's only stated month-to-day conversion and cl.20 is met on every day compared. A semi-monthly base_salary is its month; a weekly wage is taken to its month (× 52 ÷ 12) before the divisor.

encashment.authority: Labour Protection Act s.67 (as amended by No.2 B.E.2551): on termination the employer pays wages for the annual leave owed — the year of termination pro rata where the employer terminates other than under s.119, and carried-forward leave in every case — at the wage rate in force at termination. A monthly wage’s day is taken as monthly wage ÷ 30, the Act’s own conversion of a month (s.68, stated for overtime and holiday pay); no text read states another divisor for leave pay (register TH-WORK-05, TH-EXIT-02).

work_rules.authority: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 (Council of State consolidation through No.9 B.E.2568, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/ZGN3NXk0eENvNjBSdjRnT2NsdjFTQT09): s.23 normal hours at most eight a day (seven for work declared hazardous on dated employment terms); s.28 a weekly holiday; s.29 a traditional holiday falling on a weekly holiday moves to the next working day (SUBSTITUTE); s.56 weekly-holiday wages are owed except to employees paid daily, hourly or by piece; traditional and annual holidays are paid to all; s.61 overtime on a working day at least 1.5× the hourly rate; s.62 work on a holiday — (1) at least 1× more for an employee entitled to wages on that holiday, (2) at least 2× for one who is not (weekly holiday of a daily/hourly-paid employee); s.63 overtime on a holiday at least 3×; s.65(1)/s.66 an employee with authority to hire, reward or dismiss has no s.61–63 entitlement (read as work classification MANAGERIAL); s.65(2)–(9) (re-read 30 Sep 2026 in the consolidation) have no s.61 overtime or s.63 holiday-overtime pay unless the employer agrees, but keep s.62 holiday-work pay, and those in (3)–(9) are paid the working-day hourly rate for each hour worked beyond the normal hours: work classification COMMISSION_SALES (s.65(2), canvassing sales paid commission) is priced by band S65-OT-EXCLUDED at nothing and OVERTIME_AT_HOURLY_RATE (s.65(3)–(9): railway train operations, water gates, water-level reading, firefighting and public-danger prevention, outside work whose hours cannot be fixed, watch duty outside normal work, work a Ministerial Regulation adds) by band S65-OT-HOURLY-1.0X at 1× (register TH-WORK-06); an agreed higher rate is contractual, not modelled; s.68 the hourly rate of a monthly-paid employee is the monthly wage ÷ (30 × normal hours a day). The Act states no part-month proration: the seed prorates a monthly wage on calendar days, because s.56(1) pays a monthly wage for every day including weekly holidays, and deducts an unpaid day at the month’s calendar-day rate — a reading, not statute text (register TH-WORK-05). No statutory night premium exists (register TH-WORK-07). The Ministerial Regulation No.3 B.E.2541 combined 36-hour weekly overtime/holiday-work ceiling is transcribed; the timed s.27 adult breaks still need a saved compliance gate (register TH-WORK-07).

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for a s.119 cause stated in the notice
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.119: no severance where the dismissal is for dishonesty or an intentional crime against the employer, wilful damage, serious negligence, a breach after a valid written warning, three consecutive working days’ absence without reason, or final imprisonment — and the cause was stated in the notice. s.67 then pays only carried-forward annual leave.

exit_facts.label: Fixed-term project, occasional or seasonal work finished within two years
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.118 paras 3–4: severance is not owed at the end of a written fixed-term contract for a special project outside the employer’s normal business, or for occasional or seasonal work, finished within two years. Every other contract expiry is a termination (s.118 para 2).

exit_facts.label: Objected in writing to a workplace relocation (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 para.3: within 30 days of the relocation notice (or of the move), the employee told the employer in writing that the move materially affects their or their family’s life and did not go; the contract ends on the move and special severance of at least the s.118 rate is owed. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Relocation notice posted 30 days ahead (s.120)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.120 paras 1–2: the employer posted the relocation notice at the workplace at least 30 days before the move; otherwise 30 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice to an employee who does not go. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for machinery or technology restructuring (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121: the termination follows a reorganisation of units, production, distribution or service because of machinery or a change of machinery or technology that reduces the workforce. Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: 60 days’ notice given to the inspector and the employee (s.121)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.121 para.1: the date, reason and employee list were notified to the labour inspector and the employee at least 60 days before the termination; otherwise 60 days’ last wage is owed in lieu of notice (para.2). Unrecorded is no.

exit_facts.label: Termination notice date (YYYY-MM-DD, s.17)
exit_facts.description: Labour Protection Act s.17 para.2: the day the employer gave written notice ending the contract; it takes effect on the payday after the first payday on or after it. Blank or unrecorded is no notice: s.17/1 pay in lieu then runs from the removal.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 ss.24–25: the recorded reason that dispenses with the worker’s consent for this overtime or holiday-work occasion.

work_day_facts.label: Consent exception evidence
work_day_facts.description: The document proving the continuous-work necessity, the emergency or the s.25 business classification.

work_day_facts.label: Split-break agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.27: the prior agreement to split the day’s hour of rest into shorter breaks.

work_day_facts.label: Under-18 night-work permission
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.47: when the Director-General’s written permission for under-18 night work was granted; its reference is the evidence.

work_day_facts.label: Normal-day redistribution agreement
work_day_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: the worker’s prior agreement to a normal day above eight hours within the 48-hour week.

terms_facts.label: Hazardous work
terms_facts.description: Labour Protection Act B.E.2541 s.23: work the Ministerial Regulation declares hazardous to health or safety, limited to 7 normal hours a day and 42 a week. Default false: work is hazardous only as declared.

terms_facts.label: Pregnancy status
terms_facts.description: LPA s.39/1: the dated status read before night, overtime or holiday work is allowed.
